name: Equinox Hudson Yards
who: Equinox's largest club, anchoring the Hudson Yards tower with a dedicated E by Equinox training floor and rooftop pool.
why: The most recognized luxury gym brand in the US; Hudson Yards is its architectural showcase and a status symbol for Manhattan members.

name: Dogpound
who: Invite-only strength and conditioning studio founded by trainer Kirk Myers, with a sister location in Los Angeles.
why: The most photographed personal-training gym in the world; actors and models train there, gated by a roughly 100-person waitlist.

name: Third Space Canary Wharf
who: Three-floor, 100,000-square-foot luxury health club with a pool, climbing wall and in-house medical centre.
why: Widely cited as the largest luxury gym in Europe; sets the bar for the UK's premium health-club format.

name: KX Chelsea
who: Private members' health, fitness and beauty club on Draycott Avenue, open since 2002 with a spa, pool and training floor.
why: One of London's original luxury gym-clubs, still a fixture for the Chelsea and Kensington set more than two decades on.

name: Siro One Za'abeel
who: 132-room fitness-and-recovery hotel inside the One Za'abeel tower, built around dedicated Fitness and Recovery Labs.
why: The world's first hotel purpose-built for training and recovery, not a gym bolted onto a hotel; a genuine trip destination for serious trainers.

name: Anatomy Miami Beach
who: Boutique strength and wellness club on Lincoln Road, co-founded by former NFL player Marc Megna, with sister locations across greater Miami.
why: Anchors Miami's fitness-and-wellness scene, drawing athletes, models and the city's wellness-influencer circuit.

name: Heimat
who: 75,000-square-foot members-only fitness and lifestyle club in Hollywood with a rooftop pool, spa and six specialty studios.
why: Billed as the first standalone luxury gym concept in LA; blends training with a social club and carries a long waitlist.

name: Ultimate Performance London City
who: Private, no-membership personal-training gym; the original Ultimate Performance location, opened 2009, now heading a nine-gym London roster.
why: Set the template for premium one-to-one fat-loss and physique coaching that UP now runs in 20-plus cities worldwide.

name: Barry's West Hollywood
who: Barry's rebuilt flagship on Santa Monica Boulevard, replacing the original 1998 La Cienega studio with a larger Red Room.
why: The birthplace of the 'world's best workout' brand and celebrity-favorite HIIT franchise; still its cultural home base.

name: Lanserhof at The Arts Club
who: Six-floor medical gym and wellness clinic inside The Arts Club, with an in-house MRI, cryotherapy and a Spine Lab.
why: Billed as the world's first medical gym; brings Lanserhof's German longevity-clinic model into a private London institution.

name: Tracy Anderson Studio New York
who: Flagship studio of Tracy Anderson's branded dance-cardio method, which now runs ten studios worldwide.
why: Built the celebrity-trainer-to-global-method playbook; the studio her A-list clientele and the tabloids still associate with the brand.

name: Saint Haven Collingwood
who: Members-only luxury wellness and social club combining strength training, recovery labs and a lounge-and-dining floor.
why: Built a reported 15,000-person waitlist; the clearest sign Australia's premium fitness scene has gone full country-club, now expanding to Sydney.

name: S10 Training
who: Boutique strength studio with an onsite recovery spa and cafe, founded by trainer Stephen Cheuk.
why: A go-to for entertainment-industry clients chasing single-digit body fat; small in scale but disproportionately visible via press and social.

name: Continuum Club West Village
who: 25,000-square-foot, $10,000-a-month members' wellness club in the West Village, capped at 250 members with AI-assisted biometric onboarding.
why: The newest and most expensive entrant in ultra-luxury fitness, setting a new price ceiling for what a gym membership can cost.

name: Virgin Active Collection Kensington
who: Flagship 'Collection' club on Kensington High Street with a 16-metre pool, spa and one of London's largest Dynamic Reformer studios.
why: Leads the redevelopment of Virgin Active's whole UK portfolio into a hospitality-led, studio-rich format.

name: Gymbox Covent Garden
who: Original flagship of the UK's theatrical HIIT and boxing chain, known for stunt-style class production.
why: Redefined UK boutique group fitness with dramatic class concepts (fire, black-light boxing) well before the format went mainstream.

name: SoulCycle Tribeca
who: Long-running flagship studio of the candlelit indoor-cycling chain that popularized boutique group fitness in the US.
why: Along with SoulCycle's original Union Square studio, defined the 2010s boutique-fitness boom that Barry's, Rumble and 1Rebel all followed.
reach: IG unverified for this studio; brand has scaled back to roughly 57 US locations (2026)
warning: SoulCycle has closed many studios nationwide since 2023; check this location is operating before visiting.

name: 1Rebel Broadgate
who: Flagship reshape/ride/rumble studio of the UK boutique-fitness chain, inside the Broadgate financial-district complex.
why: Pioneered London's boutique-fitness-as-nightclub format, with DJ booths, sound systems and light shows built into the workout.

name: F45 Training Bondi Beach
who: One of the earliest F45 studios, in the beachside neighborhood where the global team-training franchise was founded.
why: Ground zero for a chain that scaled to thousands of studios worldwide and went public on Nasdaq off the strength of this format.
reach: IG unverified for this specific studio; global F45 brand account is far larger (2026)

name: Rumble Boxing New York
who: Original boxing-and-strength studio from the chain founded by celebrity trainer Noah Neiman.
why: Helped bring boutique boxing into the mainstream studio-fitness category alongside Barry's and SoulCycle.
